text:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm putting a concrete proposal on the table for connection snapshot + commit tokens for midstream handoffs. Goal: allow ingress to hand off a partially-served streaming request to another proxy without redoing work or leaking KV cache state.

sam: high level sounds good. can you sketch the message flow? who holds the authoritative KV snapshot?

mira: sketch: 1) ingress takes snapshot at checkpoint N (small metadata + KV refs), 2) generates a commit token signed by ingress key with metadata: model, seqN, TTL, snapshot-id, checksum, cost-accounting-id. 3) ingress sends snapshot + token to egress candidate. 4) egress validates token, mounts snapshot read-only, continues generation. 5) on successful finish (or safe checkpoint handoff) egress emits ACK-back with token+seqM to billing/observability and upstream can GC snapshot after TTL or explicit commit ACK.

carla: two quick concerns: memory bounds (snapshots could be large if we include big KV segments) and partial side-effects in user apps. how do we avoid duplicated side-effects if egress retries?

mira: great points. proposal includes: a) snapshots are shallow: only stable KV pointers + small prefix buffers; large KV blobs remain on shared blobstore referenced by id. b) idempotency: commit token contains a monotonic handoff-id and server-side dedupe table keyed by (hand-off-id, request-id). egress must check dedupe before emitting side-effecting ops.

jon: what about backpressure/latency trade-offs? if we always snapshot at N, we add latency and thrash memory under high churn. maybe make snapshotting adaptive?

mira: yes — adaptive snapshotting: SDK signals (client) and observed queue-depth decide if snapshot-on-handoff is allowed. fallback = partial rewind: client can get last stable prefix and re-run last K tokens with deterministic seeding. for short streams, we prefer rewind over heavy snapshot.

sam: can we rely on signature-only tokens (no snapshot transfer) and let egress fetch snapshot lazily from a snapshot service? that would reduce handoff payloads.

mira: exactly what I was thinking for large workloads. two modes: inline snapshot (fast path, small) vs pointer token (lazy fetch). pointer token flow: ingress stores snapshot metadata to snapshot-service, issues short-lived pointer token; egress fetches snapshot as needed. snapshot-service enforces auth and GC.

carla: operational question — how do we surface visibility for billing and SLOs? we need token -> cost-account links and traces that survive handoffs.

mira: commit token includes cost-accounting-id and trace-ids. we also record handoff events into tracing (span "handoff.snapshot") and a lightweight handoff metric. billing can later reconcile using token fields.

jon: failure modes: if egress fails mid-continue, who retries? do we reattach to original ingress or try another egress? what about duplicate token consumption?

mira: failure rules: primary egress gets a lease for TTL. if it fails before commit, ingress/edge may try another egress using same token but the dedupe-table prevents double-side-effects; when switching egress we increment handoff-attempt counter in token metadata so observability knows retries. if token reused after commit, it's a no-op.

carla: can we get a tiny pseudo example of token payload and validation?

mira: sure — example (pseudo):
```
{
  "snapshot_id": "s-12345",
  "req_id": "r-987",
  "seq_at_snapshot": 1024,
  "hand_off_id": "h-42",
  "attempt": 0,
  "ttl": 60,
  "cost_id": "acct-44",
  "signature": "SIG(...ingress_key...)"
}
```
validation steps: 1) verify signature, 2) check ttl and attempt count, 3) verify snapshot checksum matches snapshot-service, 4) check dedupe table for (hand_off_id, req_id).

sam: ok. will need a small API on snapshot-service: PutSnapshot(meta, blobs[]), GetSnapshot(id), AckSnapshotConsumption(id, hand_off_id). Also admin GC endpoint.

devops-bot: deploy/bot: NOTE: if we land this, snapshot-service will need a capacity plan. current blobstore quota is 50GB/day free; estimate +10-30% depending on replay rates.

jon: sounds reasonable. next step: write minimal RFC section with state machine and failure matrix, plus a prototype for pointer tokens. i can take the failure matrix.

mira: thanks! i'll draft the state machine and put a short checklist for eng infra on quotas and dedupe tables. will post RFC update by EOD. :thumbsup:

carla: thanks — also add a short section about privacy: snapshots must omit any PII unless explicitly opt-in and encrypted at rest.

mira: noted. encrypt-by-default and KMS-annotate snapshot metadata.

sam: thanks all. moving to design channel later if we need wider input.
